statements.text: The widespread acquisition and deployment of AI by China has implications for the world at large. Using the power of AI, a hacker can scour a network for so-called zero-day vulnerabilities in seconds.
statements.venue: House Judiciary IP Subcommittee hearing, IP and Strategic Competition with China Part III

statements.text: New technologies like artificial intelligence can present great opportunities for creative industries to innovate, but they also present a set of challenges. Can you talk about how AI and other burgeoning technologies are affecting the music industry, and what do you think Congress can do to address these issues?
statements.venue: House Judiciary hearing, Five Years Later: The Music Modernization Act (question to witnesses)

statements.text: Now, a new technology, artificial intelligence, has emerged that has a similar potential to transform many aspects of our lives.
statements.context: Opening statement at a House Judiciary Subcommittee hearing on AI and copyright law.

statements.text: How should intellectual property be considered when Congress or the Executive Branch as a whole decides to regulate AI?
statements.context: House Judiciary Committee hearing on Oversight of the U.S. Copyright Office.

statements.text: Artificial intelligence, or AI, has changed and will continue to change the way Americans create. [...] How should American creators interact with generative AI tools? What regulations will guide our innovations as a Nation?
statements.context: Opening statement at a House Judiciary Subcommittee oversight hearing on the U.S. Copyright Office, featuring the Register of Copyrights.

statements.text: Unlike most other regulatory agencies, the Copyright Office has taken concrete steps toward studying and guiding the adoption of artificial intelligence with its guidance and Notice of Inquiry. How do you see the Copyright Office's role in AI regulation?
statements.context: House Judiciary Subcommittee hearing on Oversight of the U.S. Copyright Office.

statements.text: Using AI, one could generate political ads, convincing political ads, showing Jim Jordan endorsing Joe Biden or me endorsing Donald Trump.
statements.context: Opening statement by Rep. Jerrold Nadler at a House Judiciary Subcommittee hearing on IP and strategic competition with China, focusing on IP theft, cybersecurity, and AI.

statements.text: Patients should be able to trust that their insurer will work with doctors, not computers, to make coverage decisions for necessary care. That’s why @RepJudyChu and I wrote to @CMSGov urging increased oversight on Medicare Advantage’s use of AI in guiding coverage decisions. https://t.co/ohcFkQThXa

In recent years, problems posed by prior authorization have been exacerbated by MA plans’ increasing use of AI or algorithmic software to assist in their coverage determinations in certain care settings, including inpatient hospital, skilled nursing facilities, and home health.
statements.venue: Letter to CMS led by Reps. Nadler and Chu on AI in Medicare Advantage coverage decisions

statements.text: Generative AI may be in its nascency, but many models are already capable of creating works that—if created by a human—would be eligible for copyright protection. [...] AI undeniably will have an enormous impact on our IP systems, and it is imperative that we as the Judiciary Committee consider how best to ensure that our innovation protections remain strong even as technologies change.
statements.venue: Opening statement as Ranking Member, House Judiciary IP Subcommittee hearing on AI and IP Part III

statements.text: Some may argue, however, that denying AI-generated works protection will only incentivize applicants to conceal their use of AI altogether. How do you think we should balance the legal reasons to deny protection with that practical policy concern?
statements.context: House Judiciary Committee hearing on AI and intellectual property, focusing on IP protection for AI-assisted inventions and creative works.

statements.text: Triaging and reviewing applications requires tremendous resources even if the applications are ultimately rejected. So, why should the PTO's AI guidance have any impact on the potential flood of applications?
statements.context: House Judiciary Committee hearing on AI and intellectual property, focusing on patent protection for AI-assisted inventions.

statements.text: I applaud the Copyright and Patent Offices for taking much needed first steps to clarify what should and should not receive intellectual property protection as generative AI becomes increasingly and indelibly incorporated in our society and how we creative.
statements.context: Opening statement by Rep. Jerrold Nadler at a House Judiciary Subcommittee hearing on AI and intellectual property.

statements.text:
Today, I'm joining @RepJudyChu & @SenWarren in urging @CMSGov to increase oversight of Medicare Advantage plans’ use of AI tools and algorithms to erroneously deny coverage decisions for essential care. 
CMS has a responsibility to protect beneficiaries and prevent future AI-related harms in health care: https://t.co/7JzR2TWUmY

while artificial intelligence is not the focus of this hearing, use of generative AI in the music industry is of strong interest to this Committee, both as potential as a tool for creators and the dangers it may pose that an artist's work or likeness is used without permission or compensation. statements.text: Do you believe AI users should be allowed to create unauthorized copies of a singer's voice?

statements.text: AI technology is rapidly advancing and promises to transform our society in ways we cannot even imagine today. While AI will deliver many economic and social benefits, it also poses tremendous risks that we are just beginning to grapple with. With control of AI technology in the hands of just a few entrenched companies, it is important that we keep a watchful eye on the industry, with thoughtful regulation that will foster growth and innovation while protecting consumers.
statements.context: Opening statement by Rep. Jerrold Nadler at a congressional hearing on AI innovation and competition.

statements.text:
I’m proud to have worked with @RepJudyChu and @SenWarren to call on CMS to crack down on Medicare Advantage plans using AI to deny care.

Seniors shouldn’t lose coverage because an algorithm says so. These decisions must be made by doctors, not AI.

We need stronger guardrails to ensure AI serves patients, not a dangerous 10-year moratorium that strips states of their ability to protect them.

215 House Republicans voted to block all 50 states from protecting workers, tenants, and patients from the risks of AI for 10 years.

This includes state efforts to: 
✅Block AI from denying insurance claims
✅Ban AI rent-hiking algorithms
✅Defend workers from AI-driven job loss

While Republicans claim to support working families, time and again, they side with corporations over the needs of everyday Americans.
statements.quoted:
Republicans' “One Big Beautiful Bill" has a dangerous provision to prevent states from enacting any AI regulation of any kind for 10 years.

Commentary: https://t.co/krCZIz3gEs https://t.co/vD2XnSCMBf

statements.text:
Artists, authors, and creators are being ripped off by massive, billion-dollar companies like Open AI. This theft of proprietary information is plainly illegal, and it will devastate the American industries built upon expertise and creativity. Trump’s DOJ is out of line in its attempt to intervene in this case, and it is badly misinformed about the purpose of copyright law and allowable exceptions for fair use. America can and should lead the world in artificial intelligence without building it on theft.

https://t.co/dWZh5HzPNN

With Democrats in control of both chambers of Congress next year, we have the chance to address the growing dangers of AI. The Trump administration is attempting to empower greedy AI corporations to steal from authors, artists, and creators in the guise of “national security.” Congress must legislate guardrails to ensure America leads the world in artificial intelligence without crippling our creative industries.
